Rashi on Eruvin 54a:10:1.hebrew: אימתי שמחה וכו' בזמן - שיודע לדרוש הלכות חג בחג. דבר אחר: אימתי שמחה לאיש — אימתי אדם שמח בתלמודו? בזמן שיש לו מענה, כששואלין ממנו דבר הלכה:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:10:1.english: When does a man have joy, etc., when - [Meaning,] that he knows how to expound the laws of each festival on the festival. Another explanation: “When does a man have joy?” — When does a person rejoice in his study? When he has an answer when they ask him a matter of Halakhah.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:12:1.hebrew: שארשת - ספירת שפתיו. ״בל תמנע סלה״ — כשנתת בו דעת להוציא בשפתיו:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:12:1.english: That the request of - [This means] the utterance of his lips. “You do not withhold, Selah” — when You have given him understanding to articulate [it] with his lips.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:13:1.hebrew: זכה - אם יש לו מזל טוב, ״תאות לבו נתת לו״ — שבעוד שהוא מתאוה, באה לו תאותו עד שלא ישאלנה:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:13:1.english: [If] he is fortunate - If he has good fortune, “You have given him his heart’s desire” [applies to him] — for while he is still desiring [it], [the object of] his desire comes to him before he [even] asks for it.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:13:2.english: [If he] is not fortunate - He must pine away and suffer distress.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:14:1.hebrew: כי לא לעולם אריב ולא לנצח אקצוף - אלמא ״לנצח״ לשון עולם הוא, מדסמיך ליה. וכן ״עד עולם סלה״ — אלמא ״סלה״ לשון ״לעולם״ משמע:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:14:1.english: For I will not contend forever, neither will I be eternally angry - Evidently, lanetzaḥ is an expression of “forever,” since it is juxtaposed with it [le’olam]. And likewise, “forever, Selah” — evidently Selah signifies an expression of “forever.”

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:16:1.hebrew: שרף לצואר - שאינו מצומצם בדוחק סביב הצואר, אלא שרפוי בריוח — כך הוא נעים ומרוצה לבריות:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:16:1.english: That hangs loosely on the neck - Which is not tightly constricted around the neck, but rather is loose, with room — so too, he is pleasant and agreeable to people.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:16:2.hebrew: ונראה ואינו נראה - כשמגביה צוארו, נראה מתחת זקנו, ורוב פעמים שסנטרו וזקנו מכסין אותו. כך, אם תלמיד חכם הוא, אינו רודף לצאת ולבא בשוק, אלא יושב ומחזר על תלמודו — מתקיים בידו:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:16:2.english: And seen and not seen - When he raises his neck, it is seen from beneath his beard, and most of the time his chin and his beard cover it. So too, if he is a Torah scholar [who] does not pursue going out and coming into the marketplace, but rather sits and reviews his learning — [his study] will endure in his hand.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:17:1.english: Upon whom everyone treads - That he has no arrogance.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:17:2.english: With which everyone perfumes himself - That he teaches Torah to students.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:18:1.hebrew: כאבן זו שאינה נמחת - מפני דריסת רגלי בני אדם, כך לחייו אינן נלאין מלחזר על למודו וללמד לאחרים:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:18:1.english: Like this stone that does not wear away - [Even] from the treading of people's feet, so his cheeks do not tire of reviewing his study and teaching others.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:19:1.hebrew: לא נשתכחה - חרות משמע חקוק, ואינו נמחק לעולם. על ידי הלוחות היתה תורה חקוקה לישראל מהשתכח מהן עולמית:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:19:1.english: [The Torah] would not have been forgotten - “*Charut*” means engraved, and it is never erased. Through the tablets, the Torah would have been engraved upon Israel [so as never] to be forgotten by them.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:19:2.english: Upon the tablets - On account of the tablets, the children of Israel would have been free people.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:1:1.english: She kicked him - She kicked him.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:21:1.hebrew: ממדבר מתנה - אם כמדבר הוא, תורה נתונה לו במתנה ולא ישכח:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:21:1.english: “From the wilderness to Mattanah” - If he is like a wilderness, the Torah is given to him as a gift, and he will not forget [it].

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:22:2.hebrew: אמר - רבא: איזיל אפייסיה לרב יוסף:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:22:2.english: He said - Rava [said]: I will go and appease Rav Yosef.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:22:4.hebrew: רב יוסף סגי נהור הוה, ולא היה רואהו, והכירו בטעם היין שהוא מזגו, לפי שהיה מכיר רב יוסף במזגו של רבא מתחילה, שהיה בקי ליתן מים במדה:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:22:4.english: Rav Yosef was blind and could not see him, and he recognized him by the taste of the wine that he mixed, because Rav Yosef was familiar with Rava's mixture from beforehand, as he was expert at adding water in [precise] measure.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:25:1.hebrew: כל גיא ינשא - אף על גב דלאו גבי הני קראי כתיב, דרשי ליה: דמי שבא לידי גיא, שהושפל — חוזר ומתנשא:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:25:1.english: Every valley shall be exalted - Even though [this verse] is not written alongside these verses [in Numbers], they expound it: that one who has come to [the state of] a valley, having been lowered, is once again exalted.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:26:1.hebrew: שדורסת ואוכלת - מיד לאחר הריגתה, שאינו מקפיד על תענוגים, אלא אוכל בשר בלא תבלין, וכן שאר עינוגין:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:26:1.english: That tramples and eats - Immediately after killing it; [meaning,] that he is not particular about pleasures, but rather eats meat without spices, and likewise [with] other luxuries.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:26:2.hebrew: שמסרחת - בטיט, היינו: מי שאינו הולך אחר גבהות, לקוץ במאכלו אם לא נתבשל כל צרכו. ל"א: שדורסת ואוכלת — לאחר הריגתה אוכלת מיד, כך תלמיד חכם מחזר על תלמודו מיד כשמקבלו מרבו; מסרחת — מנבל עצמו על דברי תורה. לשון זה נראה בעיני, לפי שמצינו בכל הש"ס שדרך תלמידי חכמים להקפיד על מאכלן דרך גדולה וכבוד, ועל מלבושיהן, כדכתיב (משלי ח׳:ל״ו) ולמשנאי אהבו מות:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:26:2.english: That soils - In the mud; that is, one who does not act out of haughtiness, to be disgusted by his food if it was not fully cooked. Another explanation: “That claws and eats” — immediately after killing it, it eats [it]; so too, a Torah scholar reviews his study immediately upon receiving it from his teacher. “Soils” — he debases himself for the sake of words of Torah. This explanation seems correct in my eyes, since we find throughout the Shas that it is the way of Torah scholars to be meticulous about their food in a dignified and honorable manner, and [likewise] about their garments, as it is written: (Proverbs 8:36) “And those who hate Me love death.”

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:26:3.hebrew: לעני - לזה ששם עצמו כעני, וללישנא בתרא — ששם עצמו כעני לחזר עליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:26:3.english: For the poor - For this [person] who makes himself like a pauper; and according to the latter version — who makes himself like a pauper to go around [seeking] it.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:3:1.english: Prolong life - That you prolong [your] days.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:4:1.hebrew: חטוף אכול - אם יש לך ממון להנות עצמך, אל תמתין עד למחר, שמא תמות ושוב אין לך הנאה:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:4:1.english: Grab [and] eat - If you have money to enjoy yourself, do not wait until tomorrow, lest you die and you will no longer have [any] pleasure.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:4:2.english: For the world from which we depart - [This] is our reading.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:4:3.hebrew: כהלולא דמי - היום ישנו ולמחר איננו, דומה לחופה שהולכת מהר:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:4:3.english: Is like a wedding feast - Today it is [here] and tomorrow it is not; [it is] similar to a wedding that passes quickly.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:5:2.hebrew: ואין למות התמהמה - עיכוב, כי פתאום האדם מת:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:5:2.english: And there is no tarrying for death - [That is,] a delay, for a person dies suddenly:

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:5:4.hebrew: מי יגיד לך - אם נשאר בידם, שמא יאבדוהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:5:4.english: Who will tell you - Whether [it will] remain in their hands; perhaps they will lose it.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:5:5.hebrew: הללו נוצצין - כלומר, כשהן גדילין — גדילה פרנסתן ועושרן עמהן, ואינך צריך להדאג עליהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:5:5.english: These blossom - That is to say, as they grow up, their livelihood and their wealth grow with them, and you do not need to worry about them.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:5:6.english: And these wither - [They] die, in the sense of: “and the leaf withers” (Jeremiah 8:13).

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:8:1.hebrew: יפה - לחולי זה, וקשה לחולי זה — יפה ללב, ורע לעינים:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:8:1.english: Good - For this illness, and harmful for that illness — [for example,] beneficial for the heart, and bad for the eyes.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:9:1.hebrew: שתשמרם בבטנך - שהן שמורים בידך, שאין משתכחין ממך:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:9:1.english: That you keep them within you - That they are preserved in your possession, so that they are not forgotten by you.

Rashi on Eruvin 54a:9:2.hebrew: יכונו יחד - שאתה סודרן ומוציאן בפה, ולא בגימגום ובלחישה:
Rashi on Eruvin 54a:9:2.english: Let them be established together - That you arrange them and articulate them with [your] mouth, and not with stammering or in a whisper.
